topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Ongoing, systematic tracking of infection rates used to catch an outbreak early
entries.rationale: The infection preventionist relies on this ongoing tracking to spot a cluster of hospital-acquired infections before it grows.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: A state of near-unconsciousness in which a patient can be roused only briefly by vigorous, repeated stimulation
entries.rationale: The nurse documents this deeper level of unresponsiveness when a patient no longer rouses easily to a loud voice or light touch.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: What the nurse does when a patient's condition worsens beyond what can be safely managed alone
entries.rationale: The nurse does this up the chain of command when a concern isn't addressed after using the standard chain of communication.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Type of precaution used to protect a patient whose white blood cell count is dangerously low
entries.rationale: The nurse restricts fresh flowers and raw produce for a patient on this type of precaution after chemotherapy.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Abnormal drowsiness or sluggishness, often an early sign of a declining level of consciousness
entries.rationale: The nurse treats a new onset of this finding as a red flag warranting an immediate neuro check.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: ___ time: a clotting test used to monitor a patient on warfarin therapy
entries.rationale: The nurse holds a dose of warfarin and notifies the provider when this test comes back critically prolonged.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells that runs low when a patient is anemic
entries.rationale: The nurse trends this value after a GI bleed to decide whether a transfusion is needed.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Descriptor for a patient who is dulled in alertness and slow to respond to stimuli
entries.rationale: The nurse uses this term, one step past lethargic on the LOC continuum, when documenting a patient who rouses only briefly to a loud voice.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Patchy, blotchy discoloration of the skin caused by poor peripheral perfusion
entries.rationale: The nurse recognizes this skin change on the knees and feet as an ominous sign in a patient nearing circulatory collapse.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Pancreatic enzyme whose blood level rises sharply with acute pancreatitis
entries.rationale: The nurse trends this enzyme level, more specific to the pancreas than amylase, when acute pancreatitis is suspected.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Abnormal tingling or 'pins and needles' sensation, sometimes signaling nerve compression
entries.rationale: The nurse checks for this sensation distal to a new cast as part of a neurovascular assessment.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Category of used needles and blades that must go into a dedicated puncture-resistant container
entries.rationale: The nurse never recaps a used needle and instead drops it straight into this labeled container to prevent an accidental stick.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: ___ gap: a calculated value that helps classify the underlying cause of metabolic acidosis
entries.rationale: The nurse calculates this gap from the electrolyte panel to help the team decide whether the acidosis is from an unmeasured acid or a bicarbonate loss.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Standardized handoff framework covering Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation
entries.rationale: The nurse uses this framework to hand off a patient safely between shifts or when calling a provider with a concern.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Buffer ion the kidneys retain to compensate for respiratory acidosis
entries.rationale: The nurse expects this value to rise on an ABG as the kidneys slowly compensate for a patient's chronic CO2 retention.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Digestive enzyme that rises in the blood during acute pancreatitis
entries.rationale: The nurse anticipates this enzyme, along with lipase, will be drawn when a patient presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Protective matrix of microorganisms that forms on catheters and implants, resisting antibiotics
entries.rationale: The nurse knows this matrix is why a long-dwelling central line often needs to be removed rather than just treated with antibiotics.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Redness of the skin caused by increased blood flow through the capillaries
entries.rationale: The nurse circles and dates the border of this finding around an IV site to track whether it's spreading.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday

entries.clue: Protein that reflects how much iron is stored in the body
entries.rationale: The nurse checks this lab value, not just hemoglobin, to distinguish true iron-deficiency anemia from anemia of chronic disease.
entries.topic: Lab Values, Infection Control & Assessment Saturday
